# Data Center Operators — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

Please conduct a systematic analysis of the following 8 global data center operators across 8 research dimensions.

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | Equinix | EQIX |
| 2 | Digital Realty Trust | DLR |
| 3 | GDS Holdings | GDS |
| 4 | NTT Global Data Centers | 9432.T |
| 5 | Iron Mountain Data Centers | IRM |
| 6 | CyrusOne (KKR/GIP-owned) | (private) |
| 7 | Vantage Data Centers (DigitalBridge/Silver Lake) | (private) |
| 8 | QTS Data Centers (Blackstone-owned) | (private) |

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. Capacity Decomposition & Gross-to-Billable Ratio**
For each operator, retrieve the most recent disclosed total IT-load capacity (MW) and decompose into three buckets that sum to total: (a) operational, (b) under-construction, (c) held-for-development / land-banked. Compute the gross-MW to billable-MW utilization ratio to one decimal place and rank entities. Where operators report "IT load" vs. "critical load" vs. "gross power" inconsistently, identify which definition you used and why.

**Q2. Footprint Quality Score & Scale Intensity**
Report total operational facilities and metros served, then score each operator's footprint by Tier-1 metro concentration (% of MW in FLAP-D + Northern Virginia + Tokyo/Singapore vs. all other metros). Compute MW-per-facility for each operator and rank to flag hyperscale-build vs. retail-colo strategies. Source from latest fact sheets and 10-K / 20-F filings.

**Q3. FY2024 Segment Revenue Carve-Out**
Pull data-center-segment-only revenue (USD millions) for FY2024, stripping non-DC parent activity (Iron Mountain records management, NTT telecom parent, DigitalBridge platform fees, Blackstone non-QTS real estate). For NTT, apply the FY2024 average JPY/USD rate and disclose the rate used. Reconcile reported vs. constant-currency revenue and identify any intercompany / related-party items eliminated.

**Q4. Normalized EBITDA Margin & Quality-of-Earnings Rank**
Retrieve reported adjusted EBITDA (USD millions) and margin (%) for FY2024, then compute a "normalized" EBITDA margin after stripping stock-based comp, transaction costs, and straight-line lease adjustments. Rank the 8 entities by the gap between reported and normalized margin (smallest gap = highest quality). For private operators, reverse-engineer EBITDA from rating-agency leverage statements (Moody's / S&P) and disclose the leverage ratio and debt figure used.

**Q5. PUE by Vintage Cohort**
Disaggregate fleet-wide trailing-twelve-month PUE into two vintage cohorts: pre-2015 builds vs. post-2020 builds. Where operators report only a blended PUE, estimate the cohort split using disclosed build-year mix and note the methodology. Distinguish design PUE from operational PUE for each operator and flag inconsistencies between ESG-report PUE and CDP-filed PUE.

**Q6. Renewable Energy — Strict 24/7 vs. Annual REC Re-Score**
Retrieve the renewable-electricity percentage for the latest reporting year, then re-score under two methodologies that the model must compute side-by-side: (a) annual REC/PPA-matched (the typical claim), and (b) strict 24/7 hourly-matched approximation. Decompose Scope 2 between location-based and market-based emissions. For colo operators, flag where landlord and tenant both claim the same renewable MWh (double-count risk).

**Q7. Hyperscaler Concentration Stress Test**
Report top-10 customer concentration (% of revenue or booked MW) and weighted-average remaining lease term (WALT, years). Then quantify revenue-at-risk under a counterfactual where the single largest hyperscaler in-sources 30% of its leased capacity at lease expiry, computing: concentration × (1 − retention) × annualized rent. Rank the 8 operators by this stress metric.

**Q8. Capex Intensity & Forward Pipeline Envelope**
Pull FY2024 total capex (USD millions), splitting growth vs. maintenance/recurring. Compute (a) capex / MW-added and (b) capex / revenue ratios, ranking entities. Project the FY2025-FY2027 cumulative capex envelope implied by each operator's disclosed MW pipeline applied at its trailing 3-year historical $/MW build cost; identify the operator with the largest absolute pipeline funding gap vs. disclosed liquidity + undrawn revolver capacity.

# 64-Cell Reference Answers (Q1-Q8 parallel-built)

## Q1. Capacity Decomposition & Gross-to-Billable Ratio

**Definitional note (applied uniformly):** I use **IT-load MW (a.k.a. "critical IT power")** as the primary unit because it is the cleanest apples-to-apples basis for billable capacity. Where operators publish only "gross/utility" or "critical-load" power, I convert using disclosed PUE design points (typically ÷1.4–1.6) or use the operator's own stated IT-load. EQIX, DLR, IRM, QTS, Vantage, and CyrusOne report in IT-MW; GDS publishes "committed area" in m² + utility MW (I derive IT-MW); NTT GDC publishes mostly "gross power" in its Innovative Optical and Wireless Network IR materials and I deflate to IT-load. The "gross-to-billable" ratio in this table is defined as **(operational IT-MW) ÷ (utilized/billed IT-MW)**, i.e., a value of 1.5 means 50% of operational capacity is not yet generating revenue (vacancy + commissioned-but-uncontracted).

| # | Operator | Total IT-MW (latest disclosed) | (a) Operational MW | (b) Under-Construction MW | (c) Held-for-Dev / Land-Bank MW | Billable / Utilized MW | Gross-to-Billable Ratio | Rank (1 = tightest) | Primary Source (Tier) |
|---|----------|-------------------------------|--------------------|-----|------|----------------|------------|---------|-----------------------|

Ohio, Wales, Wisconsin) | ~880 (≈84% on operational) | **1.2** | 5 | Vantage company fact sheet Mar-2025; DigitalBridge Q4-2024 supplemental p. 9 "Vantage Portfolio Statistics"; S&P "Vantage Data Centers Issuer Credit Report" Oct-2024 (Tier 2/3) |
| 8 | **QTS (Blackstone, private)** | ~1,700 MW leased + committed (interval 1,600–1,850); Blackstone has guided to >6 GW long-term pipeline incl. land-bank | ~600 | ~700 | ~400 (additional 4+ GW land-bank not yet "developable") | ~580 (≈97% leased on operational – Blackstone disclosed >85% pre-leased on under-construction) | **1.0** | 3 | Blackstone Q4-2024 earnings call Jan-30-2025 transcript (Stephen Schwarzman & Jon Gray remarks); QTS press releases Aug-2024 & Jan-2025 (Tier 3 – partial private disclosure) |

### Ranking by Gross-to-Billable (lowest = tightest fit between built capacity and revenue)

1. **QTS — 1.0** (essentially fully leased operational footprint; growth is in pipeline, not vacancy)
2. **IRM — 1.1**
3. **EQIX — 1.2** | **DLR — 1.2** | **GDS — 1.2** | **Vantage — 1.2** (4-way tie at one decimal; ties broken at 2-dp would put EQIX 1.18 < GDS 1.21 < DLR 1.20 < Vantage 1.19)
7. **CyrusOne — 1.3**
8. **NTT GDC — 1.3** (widest uncertainty interval)

### Definition / methodology audit

- **EQIX, DLR, IRM, QTS:** Report directly in **"utilized cabinet/MW"** vs. "operational MW." Their "utilization %" is the inverse of the gross-to-billable ratio. No conversion needed.
- **GDS:** Reports operational area (m²) and committed/utilized area; I converted using their disclosed average power density of ~1.65 kW/m² (FY2024 20-F draft) to derive MW utilization. Utilization 82.4% disclosed → ratio 1/0.824 ≈ 1.21.
- **NTT GDC:** Discloses "gross power capacity" (utility supply) for many sites; I deflated by design PUE of ~1.45 to estimate IT-MW (gross 2,400 ÷ 1.45 ≈ 1,655 MW IT). This is **ND-acceptable** with explicit estimation method; interval ±10%.
- **Vantage / CyrusOne:** Mixed disclosure (press releases use "MW critical IT load"; rating reports use "leased %"). Rating-agency-stated "leased percentage" of ~84% (Vantage) and ~80% (CyrusOne) used to back into billable MW.
- **Critical-load vs. IT-load:** For DLR and GDS, "critical IT capacity" = "IT-load" (no UPS/cooling included). For NTT, parent uses "総容量" (total capacity) ≈ utility/gross. Choosing IT-MW yields conservative, comparable values.

### Key observations

- **QTS and IRM** show the tightest gross-to-billable ratio (1.0–1.1), reflecting hyperscale pre-lease discipline (QTS) and Iron Mountain's small but mature DC base; both have minimal speculative vacancy.
- **EQIX, DLR, GDS, Vantage** cluster at 1.2 — the industry's healthy "operational shrinkage" given commissioning lag and 3-month sell-down on new phases.
- **CyrusOne and NTT GDC** at 1.3 reflect (i) CyrusOne's recent aggressive Phoenix/Frankfurt phase deliveries and (ii) NTT's structurally larger development pipeline relative to the leased base, plus disclosure opacity (interval-widening factor).
- The ratio is **not** a quality signal in isolation: a 1.0 ratio could indicate under-investment in pipeline, while 1.3 with a high pre-lease % on (b) under-construction (e.g., QTS pre-leases ~85% before delivery) is a stronger growth posture.

### Source-tier legend

- **Tier 1:** SEC 10-K / 20-F or audited supplemental.
- **Tier 2:** Issuer fact sheet / investor day deck (un-audited but issuer-attested).
- **Tier 3:** Rating-agency credit opinion or sponsor (KKR/Blackstone/DigitalBridge) earnings call (private operators).

### ND (non-disclosed) handling

For NTT GDC and CyrusOne, where IT-MW is not directly stated, I (i) used parent or sponsor disclosures, (ii) converted gross-to-IT via PUE 1.45 (NTT) or via Moody's stated "84% leased on 900 MW operational" (CyrusOne), and (iii) flagged interval bounds in the table. No counterfactual P&L is computed (Q1 does not request one), and no intercompany eliminations apply at the capacity-MW layer.

---

## Q2. Footprint Quality Score & Scale Intensity

**Definitions used.** "Operational facilities" = stabilized + operating IBX/colocation buildings disclosed on company fact sheets / 10-K / 20-F (excludes pure land sites). "Metros" = distinct city/MSA labels used by the operator. "Tier-1 MW" defined as IT-load MW physically located in **FLAP-D** (Frankfurt, London, Amsterdam, Paris, Dublin) **+ Northern Virginia (Ashburn/Loudoun)** **+ Tokyo + Singapore**. Where an operator's facility-level MW is not disclosed, Tier-1 share is estimated by (i) building-count share inside Tier-1 metros applied to fleet operational MW, then (ii) cross-checked against disclosed metro power tables. Source tiers: **T1** = SEC/EDINET filing; **T2** = company fact sheet/IR deck; **T3** = rating-agency or sponsor disclosure; **T4** = press/industry tracker (datacenterHawk, Synergy, S&P 451). ND = not disclosed.

² GDS Tier-1 share is 0% under the strict FLAP-D + NoVA + TYO + SG definition. If "Tier-1 APAC" were redefined to include Beijing/Shanghai/Shenzhen/HK, GDS' Tier-1 share would rise to >85%.

### Ranking by MW-per-facility (hyperscale-build vs. retail-colo gradient)

1. **Vantage** ~41 MW/campus — purest hyperscale
2. **QTS** ~34 MW/fac
3. **CyrusOne** ~18 MW/fac
4. **IRM DC** ~9.6 MW/fac
5. **NTT GDC** ~9.4 MW/fac
6. **Digital Realty** ~8.5 MW/fac
7. **GDS** ~6.0 MW/fac
8. **Equinix** ~4.3 MW/fac — purest retail/interconnection colo

This spread (4.3 → 41 MW/fac, ~9.5×) is the cleanest single-metric proxy for retail-colo vs. hyperscale-build orientation in the set. Equinix's strategy is structurally validated by the figure (interconnection density per IBX matters more than raw MW); Vantage and QTS at the top are private-sponsor-funded hyperscale platforms whose unit economics rely on >30 MW per campus to amortize substation and dark-fiber capex.

### Ranking by Tier-1 metro concentration (top to bottom)

IRM DC (55–60%) > CyrusOne (50–55%) > Vantage (48–52%) > QTS (45–50%) > Digital Realty (44–48%) > Equinix (38–42%) > NTT GDC (30–35%) > GDS (0% strict / >85% on China-adjusted definition).

IRM's elevated Tier-1 share is a consequence of its "fewer-but-larger" build pattern (VA-cluster dominates), whereas Equinix's lower share reflects its global metro diversification (73 metros) — a quality, not a deficiency, when paired with interconnection density.

### Methodology notes & ND handling

- **Equinix sellable vs. utility MW**: 10-K reports utility capacity; sellable IT MW estimated at ~70% of utility per the company's standard 1.43 PUE design (Q4'24 ESG appendix). Used sellable for MW/facility to keep cross-operator comparability with wholesale peers reporting "critical IT MW."
- **NTT GDC**: parent NTT Inc. reports the segment in JPY without facility-level MW; operational MW reconstructed from the NTT GDC global fact sheet (March 2025) and triangulated against datacenterHawk Q4'24 (T4).
- **CyrusOne / Vantage / QTS**: facility and MW counts pulled from sponsor disclosures and rating-agency reports; estimation method = direct fact-sheet read + S&P/Moody's/Fitch cross-check. Intervals shown where rating-agency MW differs from fact-sheet MW by >5%.
- **GDS**: "committed area in service" is the company's preferred metric (m² → MW conversion at GDS' disclosed 1.40 design PUE and ~190 W/ft² average) — used 661 MW operational from the Q4'24 release Table 5; SEA platform (GDS-I) added at the disclosed contracted IT load.
- **Tier-1 MW** for all operators is an **interval estimate** because no operator publishes a metro-by-metro MW table at the granularity required; intervals reflect ±3pp uncertainty from MW-per-building variance within Tier-1 metros.

**Cohort dispersion.** Across the eight operators the post-2020 cohort clusters tightly at 1.22–1.32, reflecting industry convergence on indirect-evaporative or rear-door-heat-exchanger cooling at design points of 1.20–1.25 and operational PUE 5–10 bps above design. **Design vs operational gap.** The systematic gap between design and operational PUE ranges from ~5 bps (GDS, where Chinese provincial regulators audit to load) to ~25 bps (NTT, where legacy halls in Japan run partial-load year-round and humidity drives reheat). Operators with retail/colo halls (Equinix, IRM, parts of DLR) show wider gaps than wholesale/hyperscale operators (Vantage, CyrusOne, QTS) because partial-load operation is structural, not transient.

**ND handling summary.** For private operators (CyrusOne, Vantage, QTS) and for NTT GDC where FY2024 ESG is not yet released as of 2026-04-30, fleet PUE is anchored to most recent disclosed figure and rolled forward only where a published build-year MW mix supports a residual back-out. ### Cross-cutting observations

1. **Annual ≠ 24/7.** Every operator that claims ≥95% annual matching falls to roughly **30–55%** under a strict hourly-matched test, reflecting that wind/solar capacity factors cap firm renewable supply at ~25–45% absent storage or geographic diversity. Only Iron Mountain (Constellation EnergyTag PPA) has structurally moved meaningful volume toward true 24/7.
2. **Geographic asymmetry.** US (PJM, ERCOT) and Nordics rate well on hourly tests; Singapore, Japan, Inner-Mongolia China, and India rate poorly because grids are fossil-heavy and PPA markets are nascent. This is why GDS and NTT score lowest on the hourly re-score even though their annual matching claims appear respectable.
3. **Double-count / colo flag.** Equinix, Digital Realty, NTT, and QTS host hyperscalers (MSFT, GOOG, META, AWS, ORCL) that publicly claim 100% renewable energy on **the same MWh** the colo provider also claims. GHG Protocol Scope 2 guidance (§7.5) does not bar this contractually, but it inflates aggregate "renewable" claims. Iron Mountain's Green Power Pass and Equinix's Green PPA Pass-through partially mitigate by transferring the attribute to the tenant — but operators still report the % at the corporate level, creating a measurement overlap rather than physical double-procurement.
4. **Scope 2 location vs. market gap** is the most reliable indicator of REC reliance: the larger the gap, the more of the "renewable %" is paper certificates rather than direct displacement. Equinix (gap ~92%), QTS (gap ~100%), and DLR (gap ~63%) sit at the high end; GDS (gap ~37%) lower because Chinese GEC supply is constrained.
5. **ND-acceptable handling.** For CyrusOne, Vantage, and QTS, market-based Scope 2 is not separately audited; figures are estimated from KKR/Blackstone/DigitalBridge sponsor ESG reports and triangulated against capacity × regional grid factor (EPA eGRID 2023, EEA 2024). All such cells are flagged T3/T4 with intervals rather than point estimates.

If it conflates bases across operators (e.g., gross MW for NTT vs. IT-MW for EQIX, then ranks the ratios), **cap the entire Q1 score at 0.5** for affected cells.
2. **Ratio not to one decimal.** Question requires one-decimal precision. Integer or two-decimal-only without one-decimal rounding → **−0.25 on that cell** (floor 0).
3. **Citation entirely missing.** Any cell with no source attribution is **capped at 0.5**, regardless of numeric accuracy. Generic "company website" without filing/date/page reference also caps at 0.5.
4. **ND handling without method (NTT, CyrusOne, Vantage, QTS).** Where a private/opaque operator's MW is asserted as a point estimate with no PUE-deflation, no leased-% back-out, or no rating-agency anchor disclosed → **cap at 0.25** (per the standing "ND with no method = 0.25" rule).
5. **Decomposition non-additivity.** If (a) + (b) + (c) does not reconcile to disclosed total within ±2%, **−0.25 on that cell** even if the headline total is correct.
6. **Ranking error.** The final ranking by ratio is part of the deliverable; if individual cells are correct but the ranked list contradicts them (e.g., places NTT at 1.0), **−0.25 applied to the final-ranking line item only** (not propagated to per-entity cells).

# 56_datacenters — Data Center Operators Analysis

**Normalization used:** IT-load / critical-load MW where disclosed. Where only floor area or cabinets were disclosed, I converted to IT MW and marked as estimated. Gross MW = operational + under construction + held-for-development. Billable MW = utilized / leased operational MW. ## Q1. Capacity Decomposition & Gross-to-Billable Ratio

GDS discloses **613,583 sqm in service**, **102,691 sqm under construction**, and **388,922 sqm held for future development**. NTT discloses **2,000 MW+ critical IT load** but not bucket detail. Equinix discloses major projects, cabinet additions, xScale MW and land that could support ~1 GW, but not total IT load directly.

## Q3. FY2024 Data-Center Segment Revenue

## Q5. PUE by Vintage Cohort

| QTS | ~1.32 | 1.45 | 1.24 | QTS discloses WUE and carbon-free energy more clearly than PUE in public summaries. |

CDP / ESG inconsistency risk: highest for operators mixing design PUE, operating PUE and tenant-energy boundaries. CyrusOne is clear that its 2024 sustainability report covers 2023 performance.

## Q6. Renewable Energy: Annual REC/PPA vs Strict 24/7

| Operator | Reported annual renewable / CFE | Strict 24/7 estimate | Scope 2 location-based | Scope 2 market-based | Double-count risk |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|

| QTS | **100% operational CFE** | 45% | ~0.22 MtCO2e | ~0.0 MtCO2e | High for single-tenant facilities |

Strict 24/7 is my computed approximation: annual matched MWh multiplied by an hourly-deliverability factor by region and procurement type. Annual REC/PPA claims are not equivalent to hourly carbon-free consumption.

## Q7. Hyperscaler Concentration Stress Test

Formula: **largest hyperscaler concentration × 30% in-sourcing × FY2024 DC revenue**.

Equinix has the lowest concentration risk despite its scale because revenue is diversified across retail colo, interconnection and enterprise customers.

Q1.rationale: Capacity decompositions and gross-to-billable ratios are mostly far from the reference, often inflating land-bank or total capacity and computing ratios around 2x-6x instead of 1.0x-1.3x. Only NTT gets minimal credit for acknowledging opacity and a rough critical-load basis, though the method and ratio are still wrong.

Q2.rationale: Digital Realty is broadly aligned on facilities, metros, Tier-1 share, MW/facility, and strategy. Most other entities have materially wrong MW/facility, Tier-1 concentration, or facility/metro counts, though several preserve the rough strategy direction.

Q3.rationale: Public-company revenue figures are partly correct, especially IRM, but constant-currency and elimination details are often missing or wrong. Private-company estimates for Vantage and QTS are materially incorrect, and GDS misses the required DayOne and related-party treatment.

Q4.rationale: Equinix is directionally close, but most normalized EBITDA gaps are materially understated and add-back bridges are incomplete. Private-operator EBITDA figures lack the required leverage-and-debt reverse-engineering, with Vantage and QTS especially far from the reference.

Q5.rationale: The answer generally captures that newer cohorts should have lower PUE than pre-2015 cohorts, but it often lacks the required residual methodology, design-vs-operational clarity, and ESG/CDP reconciliation. NTT and CyrusOne are notably off on blended PUE and disclosure handling.

Q6.rationale: Annual versus 24/7 matching is presented side-by-side, but many 24/7 estimates and Scope 2 splits are materially outside the reference bands. Double-count risk is usually flagged, but several key methodology details and regional/PPA specifics are missing.

Q7.rationale: The formula is stated, but most concentration, WALT, and revenue-at-risk values are materially off, especially QTS, Vantage, DLR, and IRM. CyrusOne earns partial credit because the largest-customer share and revenue-at-risk are close despite weak sourcing detail.

Q8.rationale: Capex, capex/MW, envelopes, and funding gaps are largely wrong, and the answer incorrectly identifies Digital Realty rather than QTS as the largest funding gap. Equinix receives only minimal credit for a total capex figure within the loose range while the envelope and gap are badly overstated.

I have sufficient research. Let me now write the final answer synthesizing all the gathered evidence with appropriate uncertainty flags.

# Data Center Operators — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

**Methodological note.** Capacity and financial disclosures across these 8 operators are not standardized. Equinix, DLR, GDS, IRM, and NTT publish in SEC/TSE filings; CyrusOne, Vantage, and QTS are private, so their disclosures come from rating-agency presales (S&P), ABS/CMBS offering documents, sponsor press releases (Blackstone/DigitalBridge/KKR), and fact sheets. Where a metric is not disclosed, I flag it as **ND** and provide an estimate with the derivation. I use **IT-load MW** (net critical IT power) as the common denominator wherever possible, since gross/utility power is reported inconsistently (Vantage/QTS lean toward "expected capacity" incl. electrical headroom; Equinix/GDS report "power capacity in service"; DLR reports "utility capacity" and "IT load"). I explicitly note which definition each operator uses.

---

## Q1. Capacity Decomposition & Gross-to-Billable Ratio

Values are most-recently-disclosed year-end 2024 (or closest available), in MW of IT load unless noted.

| # | Operator | Definition used | (a) Operational MW | (b) Under-construction MW | (c) Held-for-dev / land-bank MW | Total MW | Billable / utilized MW | Gross-to-Billable ratio |
|---|----------|-----------------|-------------------:|--------------------------:|--------------------------------:|---------:|-----------------------:|------------------------:|
| 1 | Equinix | IBX "operating" cabinets + xScale MW; powered land pipeline | ~1,800 (operating IBX + xScale live) | ~400 (62 projects, 16 xScale, adds 34k cabinets + >165 MW by YE26) | ~800 (powered land; ~3 GW "developable" per CEO) | **~3,000** | ~1,500 billable (~82% retail utilization) | **2.0** |
| 2 | Digital Realty (DLR) | "IT load" (UPS-backed white-space) in 10-K | ~2,600 (308 DCs, 84.1% leased) | ~785 (344 MW at 3Q24 × ~2x) | ~2,500 (land/utility for future) | **~5,900 IT load; ~3.0 GW utility capacity operational** | ~2,190 (84.1% of operational) | **2.7** |
| 3 | GDS (China + DayOne intl.) | "Power capacity in service" / under construction | 132 (China) + ~150 DayOne = **~282** | 369 China + ~320 DayOne ≈ **~690** | ~600+ (590 MW DayOne held-for-dev) | **~1,570** | 123 MW utilized (China) + ~260 DayOne committed ≈ **~383** | **4.1** |
| 4 | NTT Global Data Centers | "IT capacity" | ~1,500 | ~380 added FY24; >1 GW pipeline across 7 mkts | ND (est. ~1–2 GW land) | **~3,000–4,000** | ND (est. ~1,200 utilized) | **2.5–3.3** |
| 5 | Iron Mountain (IRM) Global DC | "MW capacity" (leasable) | ~285 (97% leased of "existing ~290 MW" as of FY24; 488 MW incl. new builds by 2025) | ~160 (162 MW at 3Q24) | ~300+ (VA7 JV, London, Frankfurt, Chennai 42 MW etc.) | **~750** | ~277 (97% of 285) | **2.7** |
| 6 | CyrusOne (KKR/GIP) | "IT load" per KKR | ~1,000 (≈55 DCs × ~18 MW) | ~500+ (144 MW TX ECP, 190 MW TX, 200 MW Fort Worth) | ~1,500+ (Illinois 600 MW site etc.) | **~3,000** | ~900 (est. ~90% leased) | **3.3** |
| 7 | Vantage (DigitalBridge/Silver Lake) | "Expected capacity" (gross) | ~750 (35 campuses, ~415 MW US operational per 3rd-party; global ≥750 MW) | ~800+ | ~1,100 | **~2,600 (planned + existing, per co.)** | ~700 | **3.7** |
| 8 | QTS (Blackstone) | "IT load" / leased capacity | ~1,400 (disclosed 107.5 MW single ABS + 215 MW CMBS trio + remainder) | ~800+ | ~900+ (Britishvolt 750 MW, PA sites) | **~3,000+ (Blackstone notes "more than 3 GW" by 2026)** | ~1,350 (Blackstone says "fully-leased") | **2.2** |

**Ranking by gross-to-billable ratio (smallest = most efficient monetization of owned capacity):**
1. Equinix 2.0 → 2. QTS 2.2 → 3. NTT 2.5–3.3 → 4. DLR 2.7 (tie IRM 2.7) → 6. CyrusOne 3.3 → 7. Vantage 3.7 → 8. GDS 4.1

## Q5. PUE by Vintage Cohort — Pre-2015 vs Post-2020 Builds

**Methodology note:** Where only a blended PUE is reported, the cohort split was estimated using two inputs: (i) the operator's mix of capacity by vintage (disclosed in ESG or 10-K vintages) and (ii) published engineering design norms of ~1.5 for pre-2015 air-cooled and ~1.2 for post-2020 hot-aisle-contained/liquid-cooled builds. The vintage split is approximate: EQIX has ~30% pre-2015 legacy, DLR ~40%, GDS/Vantage <10% (both operators are <15 yrs old), IRM Global DC is mostly post-2018.

**ESG-vs-CDP discrepancy flag:** Equinix reports 1.39 in both its 2024 sustainability report and its CDP C2024 filing. DLR does **not** publish a global fleet-wide PUE in its 2024 Impact Report — only regional and "Exceeded 5% improvement in NA" is mentioned, which is a transparency gap vs CDP. Vantage and QTS do not publish CDP responses publicly.

**Sources:** Equinix Sustainability page (sustainability.equinix.com); DLR 2024 Impact Report; GDS 20-F 2024; CyrusOne Sustainability Report 2024 (PDF); IRM 2024 10-K ESG disclosures; NTT Data Integrated Report FY2024; holdfastprojects.com US DC PUE benchmark.

## Q6. Renewable Energy — Annual REC vs Strict 24/7 Hourly Re-Score

| # | Operator | Annual REC/PPA match % (co. claim) | Strict 24/7 hourly est. | Scope 2 location-based (tCO2e) | Scope 2 market-based (tCO2e) | Double-count flag |
|---|----------|-----------------------------------:|------------------------:|-------------------------------:|----------------------------:|-------------------|
| 1 | EQIX | **96%** renewable in 2024 retail IBX | **~55%** (heavy US/APAC unbundled RECs) | ~4.0 M | ~0.4 M | Medium: colo tenants also claim |
| 2 | DLR | **64%** utility incl. + 100% "coverage" where contracted | **~45%** | ~3.2 M | ~1.0 M | High: wholesale tenants routinely re-claim |
| 3 | GDS | **~36%** (grid) + 25%+ PPA | **~30%** | ~4.5 M | ~3.0 M | Low: China tenants rarely claim |
| 4 | NTT GDC | **~35%** global; Japan sites ~20% | **~25%** | ~3.5 M | ~2.3 M | Medium |
| 5 | IRM | **100%** (Green Power Pass; founding signatory UN 24/7 Compact) | **~65%** (stronger than peers) | ~0.9 M | ~0.05 M | Low (IRM shares 24/7 reporting) |
| 6 | CyrusOne | **100%** (claim since 2021 via unbundled RECs) | **~40%** | ~1.8 M | ~0 reported | **High**: many tenants also claim |
| 7 | Vantage | **~85%** claimed | **~40%** | ~1.5 M | ~0.3 M | High |
| 8 | QTS | **100%** claim via RECs | **~40%** | ~2.5 M | ~0 reported | **High** |

**Methodology:** Strict 24/7 approximation = (renewable MWh coincident with load) / (total MWh). Since only IRM and (partially) Equinix disclose hourly matching, I applied a haircut based on geography: for each operator I assumed 80% coincidence in US/EU grids with solar-dominant PPAs, 30% in APAC, 50% in Nordic hydro markets, weighted by disclosed regional MWh split. This is a model, not an audited figure.

**Double-count risk:** Highest at wholesale/hyperscale providers (DLR, CyrusOne, QTS, Vantage) where the colo landlord claims the REC for Scope 2 market-based reporting AND the hyperscaler tenant claims the same MWh in its own corporate renewable accounting (Amazon, Microsoft, Meta all claim supplier PPAs). IRM's Green Power Pass is the only program with explicit chain-of-custody to prevent tenant double-counting.

**Sources:** Equinix sustainability page; DLR 2024 Impact Report; IRM 2024 sustainability disclosures (UN 24/7 Compact founding signatory); CyrusOne Sustainability Report 2024; Vantage reports/brochures page; QTS Blackstone sustainability letter.

---

## Q7. Hyperscaler Concentration Stress Test

Counterfactual: largest hyperscaler insources **30%** of leased capacity at expiry. Revenue-at-risk = Top-1 customer % × 30% × annualized rent.

| # | Operator | Top-10 % revenue | WALT (yrs) | Top-1 % rev (est.) | Revenue-at-risk (30% insource, $M) | Rank |
|---|----------|-----------------:|-----------:|-------------------:|-----------------------------------:|-----:|
| 1 | EQIX | ~15% | ~2.5 (retail) / 7 (xScale) | ~3% (no 10% cust.) | 8,748 × 3% × 30% = **$79** | 1 (lowest risk) |
| 2 | DLR | ~51% (top-20) | ~4.6 | ~12% (Fortune-50 SW co.) | 5,555 × 12% × 30% = **$200** | 5 |
| 3 | GDS | ~70% top-10 | ~6.2 | ~30% (Alibaba/Tencent) | 1,485 × 30% × 30% = **$134** | 3 |
| 4 | NTT GDC | ~40% | ~5 | ~10% | 2,000 × 10% × 30% = **$60** | 2 |
| 5 | IRM | ~60% | ~10 (long hyperscale) | ~20% | 620 × 20% × 30% = **$37** | 8 (lowest absolute) |
| 6 | CyrusOne | ~75% | ~6 | ~25% (Top-3 are hyperscalers) | 1,700 × 25% × 30% = **$128** | 4 |
| 7 | Vantage | ~85% | ~8 | ~30% (single hyperscaler dominant in N.VA) | 900 × 30% × 30% = **$81** | 6 |
| 8 | QTS | ~85%+ | ~10 (preleased mega-deals) | ~35% (one hyperscaler >$22 B preleased pipeline) | 1,800 × 35% × 30% = **$189** | 7 |

**Ranked by absolute revenue-at-risk ($M):** DLR 200 > QTS 189 > GDS 134 > CyrusOne 128 > Vantage 81 > EQIX 79 > NTT 60 > IRM 37.

**Ranked by % of total revenue at risk (intensity):** QTS (10.5%) > Vantage (9.0%) > GDS (9.0%) > CyrusOne (7.5%) > IRM (6.0%) > NTT (3.0%) > DLR (3.6%) > EQIX (0.9%).

Equinix has by far the lowest hyperscaler concentration risk (no single customer is 10%+ and diversified 10,000+ customers). QTS/Vantage are most exposed due to preleased mega-deals to single hyperscalers.

**Sources:** EQIX 10-K 2024 ("no one customer 10%+"); DLR 10-K 2024 ("top 20 = 51% of ARR"); GDS 20-F 2024 (discloses Alibaba/Tencent concentration); S&P presales for CyrusOne and Vantage (tenant concentration schedules). Where undisclosed, I used peer-group averages and flagged as estimate.

---

## Q8. Capex Intensity & Forward Pipeline Envelope

### FY2024 capex (USD millions)

| # | Operator | Total capex | Growth capex | Maint./recurring | Capex / MW added | Capex / Revenue |
|---|----------|------------:|-------------:|-----------------:|-----------------:|----------------:|
| 1 | EQIX | 3,403 | ~3,180 | ~220 | ~$12 M/MW (282 MW added) | 38.9% |
| 2 | DLR | ~3,300 | ~3,150 | ~150 | ~$11 M/MW (~300 MW) | 59.4% |
| 3 | GDS | ~$1,000 (US$ eq.) | ~$950 | ~$50 | ~$10 M/MW (~100 MW) | 67.3% |
| 4 | NTT GDC | ~$2,650 (¥413 B/150) | ~$2,600 | ~$50 | ~$7 M/MW (380 MW) | 132% (capex>rev, in growth mode) |
| 5 | IRM Global DC | ~$1,300 (of $1.9 B IRM total) | ~$1,250 | ~$50 | ~$13 M/MW (~100 MW) | 210% (capex>>rev) |
| 6 | CyrusOne | ~$4,500 (est. from $7.9 B RCF draw) | ~$4,400 | ~$100 | ~$11 M/MW (~400 MW) | 265% |
| 7 | Vantage | ~$3,500 (from $13 B incremental funding spread over 3 yrs) | ~$3,400 | ~$100 | ~$14 M/MW (~250 MW) | 389% |
| 8 | QTS | ~$7,000 (Blackstone disclosed ">$20 B dev. pipeline 2024-26") | ~$6,900 | ~$100 | ~$13 M/MW (~550 MW) | 389% |

### Capex / MW ranking (lowest = most efficient):
NTT (~$7M) < GDS (~$10M) < DLR (~$11M) ≈ CyrusOne (~$11M) < EQIX (~$12M) < IRM (~$13M) ≈ QTS (~$13M) < Vantage (~$14M).

NTT leads on unit cost (Asia land + power cheaper); Vantage highest (premium N.VA/FFM land + liquid-cooling retrofit).

### FY2025–FY2027 cumulative capex envelope (implied)

Using trailing 3-yr $/MW × disclosed MW pipeline:

| # | Operator | Pipeline MW | Trailing $/MW | Implied 3-yr capex ($B) | Disclosed liquidity + undrawn revolver ($B) | **Funding gap ($B)** |
|---|----------|------------:|--------------:|------------------------:|--------------------------------------------:|---------------------:|
| EQIX | ~1,200 (xScale JV + retail) | $12M | **$14** | ~$7 (cash $3.1 + $4 RCF) + $15 B JV (50%) = ~$14.5 | **~-$0.5 (covered)** |
| DLR | ~2,500 | $11M | **$27** | ~$5 (cash $3 + RCF $3 + $3 hyperscale fund) | **~$16** |
| GDS | ~690 | $10M | **$7** | ~$2 (cash + C-REIT + DayOne $1 B raise) | **~$5** |
| NTT GDC | ~1,500 | $7M | **$10** | Backed by NTT Group $200 B+ balance sheet | **~0 (covered)** |
| IRM | ~300 | $13M | **$4** | $2.5 (RCF + cash) | **~$1.5** |
| CyrusOne | ~1,500 | $11M | **$17** | $7.9 B RCF + $4 B ABS cap. = ~$12 | **~$5** |
| Vantage | ~1,800 | $14M | **$25** | $13 B equity + $7 B debt cap. = $20 | **~$5** |
| **QTS** | **~2,500+** | $13M | **$33** | $4.6 B IG bond + $20 B ABS capacity + Blackstone equity ~$10 B = $35 | **~-$2 (covered IF sponsor equity deployed)** |

**Operator with largest absolute pipeline funding gap:** **DLR (~$16 B)** — it has the biggest disclosed 3-yr capex envelope relative to ready liquidity, despite its $3 B hyperscale fund and $3 B RCF. DLR will need equity issuance + additional JV capital to close the gap. GDS, Vantage, and CyrusOne each face ~$5 B gaps.

**QTS** is heavily funded via Blackstone sponsor equity and debt capacity but requires continuous bond/ABS issuance — if capital markets seize, QTS would face >$30 B of unfunded commitments.

**Sources:** Equinix Q4-24 press release (capex guidance); DLR Q4-24 supplement; GDS 4Q24 release; NTT Group FY24 results (¥413 B DC capex); IRM 2024 10-K; Blackstone 4Q24 earnings; Vantage funding PR Jan 2025; CyrusOne $7.9 B RCF (Bloomberg Jul 2024).

---

## Summary rankings across dimensions

| Dimension | Best (leader) | Worst (laggard) |
|-----------|---------------|-----------------|
| Q1 Gross-to-billable | EQIX 2.0 | GDS 4.1 |
| Q2 MW/facility (hyperscale) | QTS ~40 | GDS 2.6 |
| Q3 DC-only revenue | EQIX $8.7B | IRM $0.62B |
| Q4 Earnings quality (gap) | NTT GDC (200 bps) | EQIX (600 bps) |
| Q5 PUE (blended) | GDS 1.29 | NTT GDC ~1.45 |
| Q6 24/7 renewables | IRM ~65% | GDS/NTT ~25-30% |
| Q7 Hyperscaler concentration risk | EQIX 0.9% | QTS 10.5% |
| Q8 Capex/MW efficiency | NTT $7M/MW | Vantage $14M/MW |
| Q8 Absolute funding gap | NTT ≈ 0 | DLR ~$16 B |

---

## Honest uncertainty / ND handling

- **CyrusOne, Vantage, QTS**: Revenue, EBITDA, WALT, and customer concentration are **not directly disclosed**. I reverse-engineered from S&P/Moody's ABS presales, CMBS disclosures, sponsor (Blackstone/DigitalBridge/KKR) investor-day releases. All such figures carry ±20% error bands.
- **NTT GDC**: The parent reports GDC as part of NTT Data's "Global" segment; ¥300 B revenue figure comes from a Q&A transcript (2Q FY24), not an audited segment. PPP conversion uses BOJ average ¥150.4/USD for FY2024 (Apr24-Mar25).
- **IRM DC segment**: 97% leased of ~290 MW reported in FY24 10-K; 488 MW is the FY25 figure that is often cross-cited — I used FY24 numbers.
- **PUE cohort splits in Q5**: Estimated from build-year mix × engineering design norms; no operator publishes audited cohort PUE.
- **24/7 matching in Q6**: Approximation; only IRM and Google publish true hourly-matched data.
- **Q8 pipeline envelope**: Implied run-rate capex assumes constant $/MW, which understates future cost inflation from AI liquid-cooling retrofits (add ~20-30% to unit cost).

**Primary sources cited:**
1. Equinix 10-K 2024 – https://investor.equinix.com/sec-filings/annual-reports/content/0001628280-25-005126/0001628280-25-005126.pdf
2. Equinix Q4-24 release – https://investor.equinix.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1063/
3. DLR 10-K 2024 – https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1297996/000155837025001424/dlr-20241231x10k.htm
4. GDS 20-F 2024 – https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1526125/000141057825000935/gds-20241231x20f.htm
5. GDS 4Q24 release – https://investors.gds-services.com/static-files/9d57b604-3a55-49bf-8be7-f95fb77dd614
6. IRM 2024 10-K – https://s204.q4cdn.com/148941814/files/doc_financials/2024/q4/IRM-2024-10K-As-Filed.pdf
7. NTT Group FY2024 results – https://group.ntt/en/ir/library/results/2024/pdf/fy2024q4kessan0509e.pdf
8. S&P Presale CyrusOne 2024-1 – https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/sourceId/13021245
9. Vantage Growth Jan-25 PR – https://vantage-dc.com/news/vantage-data-centers-growth-continued-in-2024-…
10. CyrusOne Sustainability Report 2024 – https://www.cyrusone.com/hubfs/Website%20Documents%202025/2024_CyrusOne_Sustainability_Report.pdf
11. Blackstone QTS disclosures – https://www.breit.com/investing-in-artificial-intelligence/
12. Equinix sustainability site – https://sustainability.equinix.com/environment/efficiency-and-clean-power/

Q1.rationale: The candidate states an IT-load basis but mostly computes gross-to-billable using total pipeline/land-bank rather than operational MW, producing ratios far from the reference. Several decompositions materially overstate totals or conflate DayOne/private land-bank figures.

Q2.rationale: Some facility counts and strategy labels are directionally correct, especially DLR/NTT/CyrusOne, but MW-per-facility and Tier-1 shares are often wrong or use inconsistent operational MW bases. Vantage, QTS, GDS, and Equinix have major scale-intensity errors.

Q3.rationale: Public-company revenues for EQIX, DLR, and IRM are broadly right but lack required reconciliation detail or contain wrong FX/constant-currency claims. GDS, NTT, CyrusOne, and Vantage miss key carve-outs or reverse-engineering methods; QTS is numerically close but poorly supported.

Q4.rationale: EQIX, GDS, and IRM are directionally close, but DLR and several private-operator EBITDA/leverage derivations are materially wrong. The private-company cells generally do not disclose the required debt/leverage anchors and understate the normalization gaps.

Q5.rationale: The candidate gives plausible blended/design/pre-post PUE directionality and a residual methodology, but citations and scope reconciliations are weak. NTT incorrectly says the ESG/CDP-style figures are consistent and misses the known scope discrepancy.

Q6.rationale: Annual and 24/7 figures are presented side-by-side, but many 24/7 haircuts and Scope 2 splits are far outside the reference bands. Double-count risk is often under- or misclassified, and several PPA/REC specifics are missing.

Q7.rationale: The formula is used, but many inputs are wrong, especially NTT, IRM, CyrusOne, and QTS. GDS names the wrong anchor customer, while QTS is materially understated and not correctly ranked by absolute stress.

Q8.rationale: Capex totals are sometimes near reported figures, but $/MW, capex/revenue, pipeline envelopes, and funding gaps are widely wrong. The answer incorrectly identifies DLR rather than QTS as the largest absolute funding gap, which is a central Q8 requirement.

# Data Center Operators — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

---

## Q1. Capacity Decomposition & Gross-to-Billable Ratio

### Methodology Note
Operators use inconsistent capacity definitions. Where possible, I use **IT load** (UPS-backed power delivered to customer equipment), which is the most comparable metric across the peer set. ### Double-Counting Risk Analysis

**Critical issue for colo operators:** When a landlord (e.g., Equinix, DLR) claims 96% or 100% renewable and a tenant also claims the same MWh under Scope 2 market-based reporting (via Green Power Pass or similar), the same REC is counted twice. This is a well-known structural issue in colocation:

- **Equinix** and **Iron Mountain** offer Green Power Pass products that transfer REC claims to tenants — if properly accounted, this avoids double-counting but reduces the operator's own claim.
- **Digital Realty** reports 100% renewable for NA colocation — tenants leasing space may independently claim the same renewable attribute.
- The **GHG Protocol** is currently updating its Scope 2 Guidance to address this colocation double-counting risk.

Massive capex pipelines with significant funding gaps. Strong sponsorship (KKR/GIP, DigitalBridge/Silver Lake, Blackstone) partially mitigates capital access risk |

**⚠️ Critical Limitations:** Financial data for CyrusOne, Vantage Data Centers, and QTS are **estimates triangulated from limited public sources** (rating agency presale reports, CMBS/ABS disclosures, press releases, industry databases). Actual figures are not publicly available and could differ materially. The analysis should be refreshed as these entities access public debt markets (providing more disclosure) or pursue public listings.

Q1.rationale: The answer states an IT-load preference but most decompositions are materially wrong, often using potential/gross capacity or private estimates without the required rating-agency/PUE methods. Ratios and rankings are frequently inconsistent with the rubric, with several private-company specifics unsupported.

Q2.rationale: Facility and metro counts are partly plausible for several operators, but Tier-1 shares and MW-per-facility are often wrong or based on redefined geographies. GDS silently treats China metros as Tier-1, and Vantage/QTS MW-per-facility figures are inflated by pipeline or land-bank assumptions.

Q3.rationale: Public-company revenue figures are mostly directionally correct but omit required constant-currency and intercompany/related-party reconciliations. NTT is derived from an industry yield rather than a segment carve-out, while Vantage and QTS are far below the reference ranges and lack acceptable reverse-engineering.

Q4.rationale: Several EBITDA figures are near plausible ranges, but normalization add-backs, margins, and QoE rankings are mostly wrong. Private-operator EBITDA is not properly reverse-engineered from disclosed leverage and debt figures, triggering low scores.

Q5.rationale: The answer generally captures that newer cohorts have lower PUE, but many values are loose estimates and required ESG/CDP scope reconciliations are missing. NTT and IRM fail to flag the known scope inconsistencies, and IRM lacks a clear blended fleet PUE.

Q6.rationale: Annual and 24/7 figures are presented side-by-side, but many renewable percentages and Scope 2 decompositions are wrong or missing. Private-operator Scope 2 estimates lack the required methodology, and several double-count risk flags are incomplete or misclassified.

Q7.rationale: The stress-test formula is altered by stripping annualized rent, causing most revenue-at-risk outputs to miss the required ranges. QTS is not identified as the highest-risk operator, and several largest-customer anchors and concentration figures are materially wrong.

Q8.rationale: Most capex/MW, capex/revenue, and forward funding-gap estimates are materially off, with frequent confusion between guidance, total parent capex, and DC-only capex. The answer incorrectly names Vantage rather than QTS as the largest absolute pipeline funding gap.

## Q3. FY2024 Segment Revenue Carve-Out

| 2 | **Digital Realty** | $5,555⁵⁹ | Entire company is DC operations | N/A |
| 3 | **GDS Holdings** (cont. ops) | $1,414⁶⁰ | Continuing ops only (RMB 10,322M ÷ 7.2993); DayOne deconsolidated | 7.2993 RMB/USD (Dec 31, 2024 Fed H.10) |
| 4 | **NTT GDC** | ~$1,935⁶¹ | DC colocation revenue ~¥300B (NTT DATA Q2 FY2024 presentation); ¥300B ÷ 154.9 (FY2024 avg JPY/USD per Fed) | ¥154.9/USD (FY2024 avg) |
| 5 | **Iron Mountain DC** | $620⁶² | IMDC segment per sustainability overview | N/A |
| 6 | **CyrusOne** | ~$1,400⁶³ | Est. from pre-takeout run-rate ~$1.6B (2021) grown ~15% and Moody's/S&P ABS disclosures; no public filings | N/A |
| 7 | **Vantage DC** | ~$550⁶⁴ | Est. from industry comps; private; revenue not publicly disclosed | N/A |
| 8 | **QTS** | ~$1,800⁶⁵ | Est. from CMBS portfolio ($466M revenue from 10 properties ~215 MW; total >2 GW implies ~$1.8B); Blackstone doesn't break out QTS | N/A |

**Reconciliation Notes:**
- **GDS**: Full-year continuing ops revenue RMB 10,322.1M; DayOne (discontinued) added RMB 1,262.1M. RMB-to-USD at period-end rate of 7.2993 (disclosed in earnings release). Constant-currency revenue growth was 6.3% ex one-time items.

- **Iron Mountain**: IMDC segment reported $620M revenue in the 2024 IMDC Sustainability Performance Overview. Consolidated Iron Mountain revenue was $6,150M (10-K).
- **Private operators** (CyrusOne, Vantage, QTS): Revenues estimated from rating-agency disclosures, CMBS filings, and industry benchmarks. No intercompany eliminations disclosed.

---

## Q4. Normalized EBITDA Margin & Quality-of-Earnings Rank

| # | Operator | Reported Adj. EBITDA (USD M) | Reported Margin % | SBC (USD M) | Txn Costs | SL Rent Adj. | Normalized Margin % | Gap (bps) | Quality Rank |
|---|----------|------------------------------|-------------------|-------------|-----------|-------------|---------------------|-----------|--------------|
| 1 | **Equinix** | $4,097⁶⁶ | 47.0% | ~$350⁶⁷ | $50⁶⁸ | ~$180⁶⁹ | ~41.0% | ~600 | 7 |
| 2 | **Digital Realty** | $2,291⁷⁰ | ~41.3%⁷¹ | ~$120 | ~$20 | ~$150 | ~36.5% | ~480 | 5 |
| 3 | **GDS Holdings** | $668⁷² | 47.2% | ~$25⁷³ | — | N/A | ~45.4% | ~180 | 2 |
| 4 | **NTT GDC** | ~$700⁷⁴ | ~36% | ~$40 | ~$10 | ~$50 | ~31% | ~500 | 6 |
| 5 | **Iron Mountain DC** | ~$267⁷⁵ | ~43% | ~$50 (alloc.) | ~$15 (alloc.) | ~$30 | ~36% | ~700 | 8 |
| 6 | **CyrusOne** | ~$750⁷⁶ | ~54% | ~$30 | — | ~$20 | ~50% | ~400 | 4 |
| 7 | **Vantage DC** | ~$300⁷⁷ | ~55% | ~$15 | — | ~$10 | ~50% | ~500 | 6 |
| 8 | **QTS** | ~$900⁷⁸ | ~50% | ~$25 | — | ~$15 | ~46% | ~400 | 3 |

**Methodology & Private Operator Notes:**
- **Reported → Normalized**: Stripped stock-based compensation (SBC), transaction/restructuring costs, and straight-line (SL) rent adjustments from reported adjusted EBITDA. The gap between reported and normalized margin reflects "quality of earnings" — a smaller gap indicates fewer non-cash/non-recurring add-backs inflating EBITDA.
- **CyrusOne**: Post-$15B take-private by KKR/GIP (2022), no public filings. S&P rated CyrusOne Data Centers Issuer I LLC series 2024-2 and 2024-3 (investment grade). Moody's leverage ~6.5× Net Debt/EBITDA on ~$9B debt → EBITDA ~$1.4B for the consolidated platform; ~$750M for the core DC operations after adjusting for development JVs.
- **Vantage**: $9.2B equity raise by DigitalBridge/Silver Lake (June 2024). No public debt ratings with EBITDA disclosure; estimated from industry $/MW revenue and typical 50–55% EBITDA margins for hyperscale platforms.
- **QTS**: Blackstone ownership. CMBS presale reports (DBRS Morningstar, Nov 2025) show $331.2M NCF from 10 properties (214.9 MW). Implied portfolio EBITDA ~$1.2B across the full ~2 GW+ portfolio. Leverage estimated at 5–6× per Blackstone credit disclosures.

**Quality Rank (smallest gap = highest quality):**
1. GDS (180 bps), 2. QTS (400 bps), 3. CyrusOne (400 bps), 4. Digital Realty (480 bps), 5. NTT (500 bps), 6. Vantage (500 bps), 7. Equinix (600 bps), 8. Iron Mountain DC (700 bps)

---

## Q5. PUE by Vintage Cohort

| # | Operator | Blended PUE (TTM) | Pre-2015 PUE (Est.) | Post-2020 PUE (Est.) | Design vs. Operational PUE | ESG vs. CDP Flag |
|---|----------|--------------------|---------------------|----------------------|---------------------------|------------------|
| 1 | **Equinix** | 1.39⁷⁹ | ~1.55 | ~1.25 | Design 1.20–1.30 vs. Op 1.39 | No major discrepancy; CDP A-List 2024 |
| 2 | **Digital Realty** | ~1.50⁸⁰ | ~1.65 | ~1.30 | Design 1.25–1.35 vs. Op ~1.50 | ESG report PUE slightly better than CDP |
| 3 | **GDS Holdings** | ~1.40⁸¹ | ~1.55 | ~1.25 | New builds (>2020) at 1.25 target | Limited CDP filing; uses operational PUE |
| 4 | **NTT GDC** | ~1.55⁸² | ~1.70 | ~1.35 | Design PUE 1.30 (new) vs. Op 1.55 | Not flagged |
| 5 | **Iron Mountain DC** | ~1.40⁸³ | ~1.50 | ~1.25⁸⁴ | New builds at PUE 1.3 (cool) / 1.4 (warm) per CNDCP target⁸⁵ | No major discrepancy |
| 6 | **CyrusOne** | ~1.45⁸⁶ | ~1.55 | ~1.30 | Design 1.25–1.35 vs. Op 1.45 | Not flagged |
| 7 | **Vantage DC** | ~1.50⁸⁷ | ~1.60 | ~1.30 | Target PUE ≤1.50 at >50% utilization⁸⁸ | Not flagged |
| 8 | **QTS** | ~1.40⁸⁹ | ~1.50 | ~1.25 | Design 1.20–1.30 for new builds | Not flagged |

**Methodology Note:**
Where operators report only a blended fleet-wide PUE, the cohort split is estimated using: (1) the disclosed build-year mix from sustainability reports and 10-K/20-F property schedules; (2) industry-average PUE degradation of ~0.15–0.25 for pre-2015 builds vs. post-2020 builds (per Uptime Institute data); and (3) any operator-specific retro-commissioning disclosures. For operators with significant new-build pipelines (Vantage, QTS, CyrusOne), the post-2020 cohort PUE reflects design targets.

---

## Q6. Renewable Energy — Strict 24/7 vs. Annual REC Re-Score

| # | Operator | Reported Renewable % | (a) Annual REC/PPA-Matched % | (b) 24/7 Hourly-Matched % (Est.) | Scope 2 Location-Based (ktCO₂e) | Scope 2 Market-Based (ktCO₂e) | Double-Count Risk |
|---|----------|---------------------|------------------------------|----------------------------------|--------------------------------|-------------------------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **Equinix** | 96%⁹⁰ | 96% | ~25%⁹¹ | ~700 | 253⁹² | **High** — landlord claims 96% coverage; tenants may also claim Scope 2 benefit from same grid |
| 2 | **Digital Realty** | 75%⁹³ | 75% | ~15% | ~900 | ~400⁹⁴ | **High** — 185 DCs at 100% renewable on market basis |
| 3 | **GDS Holdings** | ~20%⁹⁵ | ~20% | ~2% | ~600 | ~500 | **Low** — China grid; limited PPAs; minimal tenant overlap |
| 4 | **NTT GDC** | ~30%⁹⁶ | ~30% | ~5% | ~800 | ~650 | **Medium** — Japan/EMEA mix; some tenant overlap |
| 5 | **Iron Mountain DC** | 100%⁹⁷ | 100% | ~35%⁹⁸ | ~200 | ~15⁹⁹ | **High** — 100% clean power since 2017; expanding hourly matching |
| 6 | **CyrusOne** | ~60%¹⁰⁰ | ~60% | ~10% | ~400 | ~250 | **Medium** — EU ops at 100%; US mixed |
| 7 | **Vantage DC** | ~50%¹⁰¹ | ~50% | ~8% | ~350 | ~200 | **Medium** — campus-scale PPAs; some tenant double-claim |
| 8 | **QTS** | ~70%¹⁰² | ~70% | ~12% | ~300 | ~150 | **High** — green bond funded; landlord-tenant overlap |

**24/7 Hourly-Matched Estimation Methodology:**
The 24/7 hourly-matched score is estimated by applying a time-correlation factor to the annual REC/PPA claim. The factor reflects the fraction of RE generation that is contemporaneous (same hour and same grid) with consumption:
- **Grid-region match**: Operators with PPAs on the same grid as their DCs (e.g., Iron Mountain in EU, Equinix in select markets) score higher.
- **Geographic mismatch penalty**: PPAs in different grid regions (e.g., US wind credits applied to EU consumption) receive significant discounts.
- **Temporal mismatch**: Annual matching allows seasonal arbitrage; hourly matching does not. Typical industry conversion: ~15–35% of annual-matched RE is actually hourly-correlated (per Google/UN 24/7 CFE methodology).

**Double-Count Risk**: Flagged where colocation landlords purchase RECs/PPAs and claim 100% renewable coverage while tenants simultaneously report the same clean energy in their own Scope 2 accounts. Most acute for Equinix, Digital Realty, and Iron Mountain where market-based Scope 2 is near-zero but tenants still report grid emissions separately.

---

## Q7. Hyperscaler Concentration Stress Test

| # | Operator | Top-10 Customer Concentration | WALT (Yrs) | Largest Hyperscaler % of Rev | Revenue-at-Risk ($M)¹⁰³ | Stress Rank |

Q1.rationale: Most capacity totals and decompositions are far from reference values, often non-additive and mixing operational, pipeline, and land-bank capacity. Q3.rationale: Public-company revenue figures are often in range but generally miss required constant-currency and intercompany elimination detail. NTT and Vantage are materially wrong, while private-operator estimates lack the required leverage or margin reverse-engineering.

Q4.rationale: Equinix and GDS are directionally close, but several EBITDA figures, normalized margins, and quality rankings are materially off. Private operators mostly lack the required debt-and-leverage derivations and use unsupported estimates.

Q5.rationale: The answer attempts blended, pre-2015, and post-2020 PUE splits, but several values are stale or materially off. It also fails to flag key NTT and IRM ESG/CDP scope inconsistencies, capping otherwise plausible cells.

Q6.rationale: Annual and 24/7 figures are presented side-by-side, but most renewable percentages, hourly re-scores, and Scope 2 decompositions are far from reference values. Several double-count flags are missing, understated, or wrong.

Q7.rationale: The stress-test calculations are largely miscomputed and many concentration assumptions contradict disclosed anchors, including fabricated high Equinix concentration and incorrect QTS ranking. Only NTT receives minimal directional credit despite weak assumptions.

Q8.rationale: Several capex totals are roughly directionally plausible, but capex/MW, capex/revenue, envelopes, and funding gaps are often materially wrong. The answer incorrectly identifies Vantage rather than QTS as the largest pipeline funding gap, which is a major failure for Q8.

- **QTS:** Estimated from CMBS filings (214.9 MW at high utilization) and Moody's Baa2 investment-grade rating (Apr 2026), suggesting improving credit metrics.

**Quality-of-Earnings Rank (smallest gap = highest quality):**
1. NTT GDC (200 bps) — minimal SBC, conservative Japanese accounting
2. GDS (250 bps) — low SBC relative to revenue
3. QTS (430 bps)
4. Vantage (470 bps)
5. Digital Realty (450 bps)
6. Iron Mountain (480 bps)

**Sources:** Equinix Q4 2024 press release ($4,097M adj. EBITDA, 46.8% margin); GDS Q4 2024 earnings (RMB 4,876.4M, 47.2%); Iron Mountain Q4 2024 press release ($371M DC EBITDA); Moody's CyrusOne Ba3 upgrade; NTT FY2024 results.

## Q5. PUE by Vintage Cohort

| # | Operator | Fleet-Wide PUE (TTM) | Pre-2015 Builds (est.) | Post-2020 Builds (est.) | Design vs. Operational | ESG vs. CDP Inconsistency |
|---|----------|---------------------|----------------------|------------------------|----------------------|--------------------------|
| 1 | Equinix | **1.39** (2024 sustainability data) | ~1.55–1.65 | ~1.20–1.30 | Design PUE for new: 1.2–1.3; Operational fleet: 1.39 | CDP "A List" 3 consecutive years; no material inconsistency noted |
| 2 | Digital Realty | **~1.30** (2024 Impact Report, colocation portfolio) | ~1.55–1.70 | ~1.20–1.30 | Design PUE for new: <1.3; Older shell/core higher | 75% renewable; PUE varies by portfolio type |
| 3 | GDS Holdings | **~1.30** (China fleet) | ~1.45–1.55 | ~1.20–1.30 | Design PUE: 1.2; Operational: ~1.30 | Limited CDP filing; ESG report PUE consistent |
| 4 | NTT Global Data Centers | **~1.40** (global average) | ~1.55–1.70 (Japan legacy) | ~1.20–1.30 (new builds) | Design PUE: 1.2 for new; Operational varies by region | CDP filed by NTT Group parent; DC-specific PUE in sustainability report |
| 5 | Iron Mountain DC | **~1.30** (new builds); fleet ~1.35 | ~1.45–1.55 | ~1.25–1.35 | Design: 1.3 cool / 1.4 warm (CNDCP targets); Operational improving | ISO 14064-1 verified; CNDCP aligned; no CDP inconsistency flagged |
| 6 | CyrusOne | **~1.35** (est.) | ~1.50–1.60 | ~1.20–1.30 | Design PUE: <1.3 for new hyperscale; Operational: ~1.35 | Limited public CDP data post-privatization |
| 7 | Vantage Data Centers | **~1.25** (new hyperscale) | N/A (few pre-2015 assets) | ~1.20–1.25 | Design PUE: 1.2; Operational: ~1.25 | ESG report published; no CDP inconsistency (mostly post-2015 fleet) |

**Methodology Notes:**
- Equinix's 2024 PUE of 1.39 represents a 6% improvement from 2023 (was ~1.48). This is operational PUE across 260+ facilities.
- Operators with predominantly new fleets (Vantage, Iron Mountain new builds) show lower blended PUE.
- Vintage cohort splits are estimated based on disclosed build-year mix and typical PUE degradation curves.
- Iron Mountain explicitly targets CNDCP standards: PUE 1.3 (cool) / 1.4 (warm) for new builds at full capacity.

**Sources:** Equinix 2024 Sustainability Data Summary (PUE 1.39); Digital Realty 2024 Impact Report (75% renewable); Iron Mountain IMDC Sustainability Report 2024 (CNDCP targets); Vantage ESG report.

## Q6. Renewable Energy — Strict 24/7 vs. Annual REC Re-Score

|---|----------|----------------------|---------------------------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|-------------------|
| 1 | Equinix | **96%** | 96% (PPAs + RECs + green tariffs) | ~45–55% (est.) | ~2,500 | ~253 | Low (operator-controlled procurement) |
| 2 | Digital Realty | **75%** | 75% (PPAs + RECs; 100% in NA colo + Europe) | ~35–45% (est.) | ~2,000 | ~600 | **Medium** (tenant/landlord overlap in powered shell) |
| 3 | GDS Holdings | **~30%** (est.) | ~30% (limited PPA availability in China) | ~10–15% (est.) | ~3,000 | ~2,500 | Low (operator procures all power in China) |
| 4 | NTT Global Data Centers | **~50%** (est.) | ~50% (varies by region; Japan grid mix limits) | ~25–30% (est.) | ~1,500 | ~800 | Low |
| 5 | Iron Mountain DC | **100%** (since 2017) | 100% (annual matching with clean power) | ~60–70% (est.; pursuing 24/7 CFE pledge) | ~400 | ~0 (100% matched) | Low (operator-controlled; 24/7 CFE pledge signatory) |
| 6 | CyrusOne | **~60%** (est.) | ~60% (PPAs in US/Europe) | ~30–35% (est.) | ~500 | ~250 | Low |
| 7 | Vantage Data Centers | **~70%** (est.) | ~70% (PPAs + green tariffs) | ~35–40% (est.) | ~600 | ~200 | **Medium** (hyperscale tenants may also claim RECs) |
| 8 | QTS Data Centers | **~50%** (est.) | ~50% (green bond framework; growing PPA portfolio) | ~25–30% (est.) | ~800 | ~400 | **Medium** (hyperscale tenants may claim separately) |

**24/7 Hourly-Matched Methodology:**
- Estimated by applying typical grid carbon-free energy percentages in operator's primary markets (e.g., PJM ~35% CFE, ERCOT ~30%, Nordics ~90%, Japan ~20%) weighted by operator's geographic MW distribution.
- Iron Mountain scores highest due to explicit 24/7 CFE pledge and hourly tracking capability expansion.
- Equinix participates in 24/7 CFE initiatives but fleet-wide hourly matching remains ~45–55% due to Asian and legacy European grids.

**Double-Count Risk Flags:**
- Digital Realty, Vantage, QTS: In powered-shell/wholesale arrangements, both landlord (operator) and tenant (hyperscaler) may claim the same renewable MWh. DLR's "100% renewable in NA colo" claim may overlap with tenant Scope 2 reporting.

**Sources:** Equinix 2024 Sustainability Data Summary (96% RE, Scope 2 market-based 253,300 tCO2e); Digital Realty 2024 Impact Report (75% RE); Iron Mountain IMDC Sustainability Report (100% clean power since 2017, 24/7 CFE pledge).

---

## Q7. Hyperscaler Concentration Stress Test

| # | Operator | Top-10 Customer Concentration | Largest Single Customer (est.) | WALT (years) | Revenue-at-Risk ($M) | Stress Rank |
|---|----------|------------------------------|-------------------------------|--------------|---------------------|-------------|
| 1 | Equinix | ~15–20% | <10% (no single customer >10%) | ~2–3 (retail colo) | ~$130M | 8 (lowest risk) |
| 2 | Digital Realty | ~40–45% | ~12–15% (Microsoft est.) | ~6–7 | ~$250M | 5 |
| 3 | GDS Holdings | ~50–60% | ~20% (Alibaba/ByteDance est.) | ~5–8 | ~$85M | 6 |
| 4 | NTT Global Data Centers | ~35–40% | ~10–12% (hyperscaler est.) | ~5–7 | ~$125M | 7 |
| 5 | Iron Mountain DC | ~60–70% (DC segment) | ~25–30% (single hyperscaler) | ~10–15 | ~$56M | 4 |
| 6 | CyrusOne | ~70–80% | ~25–30% (hyperscaler) | ~8–12 | ~$108M | 3 |
| 7 | Vantage Data Centers | ~80–90% | ~30–35% (hyperscaler) | ~10–15 | ~$189M | 2 |
| 8 | QTS Data Centers | ~85–95% | ~35–40% (Microsoft per CMBS) | ~10–15 | ~$180M | 1 (highest risk) |

**Stress Test Calculation:**
Revenue-at-Risk = Largest Customer Revenue × 30% in-sourcing × (1 – retention at expiry)
- Retention assumption: 50% (i.e., 50% of capacity at risk is actually moved)
- Formula: Concentration% × Total Revenue × 30% × 50%

**Example — QTS:** 37.5% × $1,500M × 0.30 × 0.50 = ~$84M annualized. However, given long WALT (10–15 years), near-term risk is low. The stress metric captures the magnitude of potential loss.

**Rank (highest revenue-at-risk = most stressed):**
1. QTS — highest single-customer concentration + hyperscale-only model
2. Vantage — similar profile, 80–90% hyperscaler
3. CyrusOne — 70–80% hyperscaler concentration
4. Iron Mountain — rapidly growing hyperscale share (311.5 MW signed Q4 2024)
5. Digital Realty — diversified but significant hyperscaler exposure
6. GDS — concentrated but in-sourcing risk lower in China market
7. NTT GDC — diversified enterprise + hyperscale mix
8. Equinix — most diversified (10,000+ customers, no single >10%)

**Sources:** Equinix 10-K (no customer >10%); Digital Realty 10-K (~40% top-10); GDS 20-F (top-5 ~50–60%); Iron Mountain Q4 2024 (311.5 MW hyperscale signed); QTS CMBS filings (Microsoft-tied).

| 1 | Equinix | ~$3,350 | ~$3,100 (non-recurring) | ~$250 (recurring) | ~$10–12M/MW | 38.3% | 4 |

| 6 | CyrusOne | ~$2,500 (est.) | ~$2,300 | ~$200 | ~$8–10M/MW | ~208% (of DC revenue) | 2 |
| 7 | Vantage Data Centers | ~$4,000 (est. from $13B funding) | ~$3,800 | ~$200 | ~$8–10M/MW | ~222% (of est. revenue) | 3 |
| 8 | QTS Data Centers | ~$3,500 (est.) | ~$3,300 | ~$200 | ~$7.2M/MW (per CMBS filing) | ~233% (of est. revenue) | 5 |

**FY2025–FY2027 Cumulative Capex Envelope & Funding Gap:**

| # | Operator | Pipeline MW | Implied Capex ($B) | Disclosed Liquidity ($B) | Funding Gap ($B) |
|---|----------|-------------|-------------------|-------------------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Equinix | ~1,562 MW (per IR presentation) | ~$16–19B | ~$5B (cash + revolver) + JV capital ($15B CPP/GIC) | Manageable via JVs |
| 2 | Digital Realty | ~1,000 MW | ~$8–10B | ~$4–5B + JV/asset recycling | Moderate |
| 3 | GDS Holdings | ~100 MW (China continuing) | ~$0.8B | ~$1.1B cash | Manageable |
| 4 | NTT Global Data Centers | ~500 MW | ~$4B | NTT DC REIT + parent balance sheet | Manageable |
| 5 | Iron Mountain DC | ~750 MW (CNYB) | ~$6–7.5B | ~$2–3B + JVs (Frankfurt, Virginia) | **$3–4.5B gap** |
| 6 | CyrusOne | ~500 MW | ~$4–5B | $9.7B new debt (Jan 2025) + KKR/GIP equity | Manageable |
| 7 | Vantage Data Centers | ~1,800 MW | ~$14–18B | $13B+ secured in 2024 | **$1–5B gap** |
| 8 | QTS Data Centers | ~1,500 MW | ~$11–15B | Blackstone backing + $4.6B green bonds (2026) | **$5–8B gap** |

**Largest Absolute Pipeline Funding Gap:** **QTS Data Centers** — with an estimated ~$11–15B cumulative capex need against disclosed liquidity of ~$6–8B (including recent $4.6B green bond and CMBS facilities), QTS faces the largest absolute funding gap of ~$5–8B. However, Blackstone's $1.3T AUM provides implicit backstop. **Iron Mountain** faces the largest gap relative to its existing balance sheet and credit profile (~$3–4.5B gap on $13B total debt already).

**Sources:** Equinix 2025 guidance ($3.2–3.5B capex); NTT FY2024 results (¥413B DC investment); Iron Mountain 10-K (total debt $13.7B); CyrusOne $9.7B debt announcement (Jan 2025); Vantage $13B funding (Jan 2025); QTS $4.6B green bond (Apr 2026).

## Key Caveats & Uncertainty Disclosure

1. **Private operators** (CyrusOne, Vantage, QTS): Revenue, EBITDA, and capacity figures are estimates derived from rating agency reports, CMBS filings, press releases, and industry benchmarks. These should be treated as approximations (±20–30% confidence interval).

2. **NTT DC-only revenue**: NTT does not separately disclose data center revenue within the Global Solutions segment. The ~$3.5B estimate is based on industry reports and the ConvergeDigest analysis of FY2024 results.

3. **PUE vintage cohorts**: No operator publicly disaggregates PUE by build vintage. Estimates use disclosed fleet-wide PUE, known build-year mix, and industry PUE curves for different cooling technologies.

4. **24/7 hourly matching**: No operator fully discloses hourly CFE scores across all facilities. Estimates are based on grid carbon intensity in primary operating markets and disclosed 24/7 CFE program participation.

5. **FX rates used**: GDS: RMB 7.2993/USD (Dec 31, 2024 spot); NTT: ¥151.4/USD (FY2024 average, Apr 2

Q1.rationale: Most cells provide rough capacity tables, but several use wrong bases, omit land-bank buckets, or miss the required IT-load conversion and leased-percentage derivations. Iron Mountain is materially wrong by conflating pipeline/potential with leasable capacity.

Q2.rationale: The answer captures some strategy direction, but Tier-1 definitions are silently redefined, MW/facility values are often wrong, and private/opaque estimates lack adequate methods. Vantage is the closest on campus count and hyperscale orientation but still misses key anchors.

Q3.rationale: Public pure-play revenue figures for Equinix/DLR and the IRM segment are broadly right but lack required reconciliations. GDS, NTT, and private-operator estimates miss required FX, carve-out, intercompany, or reverse-engineering methodology, with Vantage materially outside range.

Q4.rationale: Equinix and DLR are directionally close but incomplete. Most other EBITDA and normalized-margin figures are materially wrong or unsupported, and private operators lack the required debt/leverage reverse-engineering.

Q5.rationale: The answer generally distinguishes older vs newer PUE directionally, but many fleet PUEs are wrong and the required residual methodology and ESG/CDP inconsistency flags are mostly missing. GDS/CyrusOne are only loosely acceptable; NTT/IRM miss known scope mismatches.

Q6.rationale: Annual vs 24/7 is presented, but Scope 2 figures and double-count flags are often wrong, especially Equinix, NTT, and QTS. Iron Mountain is directionally better due to recognizing its higher 24/7 position, though still incomplete.

Q7.rationale: The stress test uses the wrong formula by adding an extra 50% retention haircut, so most revenue-at-risk values are materially wrong. Several anchor customers, WALT values, and rankings are also incorrect or unsupported.

Q8.rationale: The answer gives capex tables and identifies QTS as the largest gap, but most $/MW, capex/revenue, envelope, and private-operator figures are outside rubric ranges or lack required trailing-build-cost methodology. IRM earns partial credit for roughly identifying DC capex and segment ratio.

**Honest Uncertainty & Not-Disclosed Handling:**

- NTT data center segment revenue is estimated from qualitative disclosures (~¥300B); exact GAAP segment reporting is not publicly available since NTT Group consolidates broadly.
- GDS DayOne (international) was deconsolidated in Dec 2024; all GDS figures here exclude DayOne for continuing operations unless noted.
- PUE cohort splits are estimated using industry-standard vintage curves where not directly disclosed.
- 24/7 hourly-matched renewable scores are approximations; only Equinix among these operators publishes a CFE score.

Q1.rationale: The answer generally conflates IT-load, gross/developable capacity, land bank, and utilization percentage, and it does not compute the requested gross-to-billable ratio to one decimal. Private/opaque estimates lack the required rating-agency or PUE-deflation methodology.

Q2.rationale: Some facility counts and strategy labels are directionally plausible, but Tier-1 definitions are silently redefined and several MW-per-facility figures are materially wrong. GDS and IRM fail core numeric bounds.

Q3.rationale: Public revenue figures for EQIX, DLR, GDS, and IRM are partly correct, but constant-currency and elimination requirements are often missing. NTT, Vantage, and QTS are materially off, with QTS far outside the acceptable range.

Q4.rationale: Only Equinix is close enough for partial credit; most normalized margins omit the required add-back bridge or use consolidated/incorrect EBITDA. Private-operator leverage reverse-engineering is weak or wrong, and several gaps are incorrectly set near zero.

Q5.rationale: The answer at least attempts cohort splits and generally preserves the direction that newer assets have lower PUE, but values and source handling are loose. It misses key ESG/CDP inconsistency flags for NTT and IRM and leaves Vantage's pre-2015 cohort essentially unscored.

Q6.rationale: Annual and 24/7 renewable scores are presented side-by-side, but most 24/7 estimates are far too high and Scope 2 decompositions are materially wrong. QTS receives no credit because annual renewable matching, market-based Scope 2, and the high double-count risk are all mishandled.

Q7.rationale: The formula is applied, and a few revenue-at-risk outputs land near the reference, but customer concentrations, WALTs, and anchor customer identities are often wrong. GDS and NTT are materially miscomputed, while QTS is ranked highest but understated.

Q8.rationale: Only a few headline capex values are near the right range; the per-MW costs, capex/revenue ratios, pipeline envelopes, and funding gaps are mostly wrong. The answer incorrectly identifies Digital Realty rather than QTS as the largest absolute funding gap.

Now I have gathered extensive evidence from multiple searches and official sources (Equinix 10-K scrape, Digital Realty 10-K scrape, Iron Mountain earnings scrape, GDS earnings scrape, Vantage press release scrape, and numerous search results). Let me compile the final answer.

---

# Data Center Operators — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

> **Methodology note:** All figures are sourced from FY2024 (calendar year unless noted; NTT uses FY ending March 31, 2025). USD conversions use the average FY2024 rate of ¥152/USD for NTT (sourced from NTT Group FY2024 results presentation). Private company data are reverse-engineered from rating-agency presales, ABS filings, and company press releases. Where data is not publicly disclosed, "ND" (not disclosed) or estimated ranges are flagged.

---

## Q1. Capacity Decomposition & Gross-to-Billable Ratio

| 3 | GDS Holdings (GDS) | ~1,070 | ~480 | ~100 | ~490 | **44.9** | IT load; China continuing ops (DayOne international deconsolidated); sqm converted at ~3 kW/sqm |

**NTT JPY/USD rate:** Used ¥152/USD (NTT Group FY2024 full-year average from financial results presentation, May 2025). At this rate, NTT DATA segment revenue of ¥4.64T = ~$30.5B total; DC portion estimated at ¥190–220B = ~$1.25–1.45B.

## Q4. Normalized EBITDA Margin & Quality-of-Earnings Rank

| # | Entity | Reported Adj. EBITDA (USD M) | Reported Margin (%) | SBC (USD M) | Transaction Costs (USD M) | Straight-Line Lease Adj. (USD M) | Normalized EBITDA (USD M) | Normalized Margin (%) | Gap (pp) | Quality Rank |

**Quality-of-Earnings Ranking (smallest gap = highest quality):**
1. Digital Realty (+3.8pp) = 2. Iron Mountain (+3.8pp) → 3. Equinix (+5.5pp) → 4. CyrusOne (+5–8pp) → 5. Vantage (+5–10pp) → 6. QTS (+7–10pp) → 7. NTT (+10–12pp) → 8. GDS (+18.1pp)

## Q5. PUE by Vintage Cohort

**Methodology:** Where operators report only blended PUE, the cohort split is estimated using disclosed build-year distribution and industry-typical PUE improvement curves (~0.03–0.05 PUE points per vintage decade). Design PUE (theoretical, at full load) is typically 0.05–0.10 lower than operational PUE (actual, at partial load).

**Flagged inconsistency:** GDS reports design PUE in ESG materials but CDP filing for Chinese operations is not independently verified. Equinix is the most transparent with both ESG and CDP-aligned operational PUE of 1.39.

---

## Q6. Renewable Energy — Strict 24/7 vs. Annual REC Re-Score

| # | Entity | Annual REC/PPA Coverage (%) | Strict 24/7 Match (est. %) | Scope 2 Location-Based (tCO₂e) | Scope 2 Market-Based (tCO₂e) | Double-Count Risk Flag |
|---|--------|---------------------------|---------------------------|-------------------------------|-----------------------------|----------------------|
| 1 | Equinix | **96%** | ~72% | ~1,100,000 | ~44,000 | ⚠️ Tenant PPAs may overlap with Equinix's 25 PPAs (1,289 MW) |
| 2 | Digital Realty | **75%** | ~55% | ~900,000 | ~225,000 | ⚠️ 1.5 GW renewable capacity under contract; tenant colocation claims may double-count |
| 3 | GDS Holdings | **~45%*** | ~30% | ND | ND | ✅ Lower risk (China REC market is separate; limited tenant PPAs) |
| 4 | NTT Global DC | **~60%*** | ~40% | ND | ND | ⚠️ NTT Group-wide renewable claims may overlap with DC-specific PPAs |
| 5 | Iron Mountain | **~70%*** | ~48% | ND | ND | ⚠️ Shared renewable claims across RIM + DC segments |
| 6 | CyrusOne* | **~55%*** | ~35% | ND | ND | ⚠️ KKR portfolio-level RE100 claims may overlap |

**Methodology (24/7 estimation):** Applied a 0.72–0.75 conversion factor from annual REC coverage to hourly-matched coverage, based on academic research showing that annual matching overstates true 24/7 carbon-free energy by 25–30% in most grids.

**Double-count risk:** Highest for Equinix and Digital Realty, where both the landlord (DC operator) and hyperscaler tenants sign separate PPAs for the same underlying renewable generation. This is a systemic issue in the colocation industry — the Uptime Institute has flagged this as a material ESG disclosure gap.

---

## Q7. Hyperscaler Concentration Stress Test

|---|--------|--------------------------------|-------------|-----------------------------|---------------------------------------|-------------|
| 1 | Equinix | ~22% | ~5.5 | ~8% (AWS) | **$56** (8% × 30% × $8,748M × 0.8 retention) | 1 (Lowest risk) |
| 2 | Digital Realty | ~28% | ~6.0 | ~10% (Microsoft) | **$117** (10% × 30% × $5,555M × 0.7 retention) | 2 |
| 3 | GDS Holdings | ~55% | ~8.0 | ~25% (Alibaba) | **$212** (25% × 30% × $1,414M × 0.6 retention) | 5 |
| 4 | NTT Global DC | ~40% | ~7.0 | ~15% (hyperscaler) | **$95** (15% × 30% × $1,350M × 0.7 retention) | 3 |
| 5 | Iron Mountain | ~35% | ~7.5 | ~12% (Microsoft) | **$64** (12% × 30% × $900M × 0.7 retention) | 2 |
| 6 | CyrusOne* | ~50% | ~8.0 | ~20% (AWS) | **$102** (20% × 30% × $800M × 0.7 retention) | 4 |
| 7 | Vantage* | ~60% | ~10.0 | ~25% (Microsoft) | **$113** (25% × 30% × $575M × 0.8 retention) | 4 |
| 8 | QTS* | ~45% | ~8.5 | ~18% (AWS) | **$70** (18% × 30% × $500M × 0.75 retention) | 2 |

\* *Private entity estimates. Retention rates based on industry averages: 80% for Equinix (strong ecosystem lock-in), 75% for QTS/IRM (contractual), 70% for DLR/NTT/CyrusOne, 60% for GDS (Chinese market pricing pressure).*

**Stress test formula:** Largest hyperscaler revenue % × (1 − retention rate at expiry) × 30% (insourcing factor) × annualized DC revenue.

**Key insight:** GDS faces the highest absolute stress ($212M) due to extreme concentration on Alibaba/Tencent. Equinix has the lowest risk due to its diversified retail-colo model and ecosystem lock-in (interconnection revenues create switching costs). Vantage and CyrusOne have higher concentration but longer WALTs provide some buffer.

---

## Q8. Capex Intensity & Forward Pipeline Envelope

| # | Entity | FY2024 Total Capex (USD M) | Growth Capex (USD M) | Maintenance/Recurring (USD M) | Capex/MW-Added ($) | Capex/Revenue (%) | 3-Yr Hist. $/MW Build Cost | FY25–27 Pipeline (MW) | Cumulative Capex Envelope (USD B) | Liquidity + Undrawn Revolver (USD B) | Funding Gap (USD B) |

1. Iron Mountain (19.5%) → 2. Equinix (35.1%) → 3. GDS (41.7%) → 4. Digital Realty (59.6%) → 5. Vantage (314%*) → 6. QTS (140%*) → 7. NTT (N/A segment) → 8. CyrusOne (100%*)

**Sources:**

- GDS Holdings FY2024 earnings release (Mar 19, 2025); Form 20-F (Apr 28, 2025)
- NTT Group FY2024 financial results (May 9, 2025); NTT DATA integrated report FY2024; ConvergeDigest analysis (May 2025)
- Iron Mountain FY2024 10-K (SEC filing 000102056925000040); Q4 2024 earnings release (Feb 13, 2025)
- CyrusOne: S&P Global Ratings presale (Series 2024-1, Mar 2024); KKR portfolio disclosure
- Vantage Data Centers: Jan 30, 2025 press release; S&P ABS presale (Series 2024-1, Oct 2024)
- QTS: Blackstone Q4 2024 earnings press release; DBRS Morningstar CMBS report (Nov 2025); DataCenterDynamics reporting (Apr 2026)

Q1.rationale: The answer reports utilization-like percentages rather than the required gross-to-billable ratios around 1.0-1.3, and most decompositions do not match the reference buckets. Several private/opaque entities lack the required rating-agency or PUE-deflation methodology.

Q2.rationale: Most facility, metro, Tier-1 share, and MW/facility figures are materially off, with GDS silently redefining Tier-1 markets and QTS badly overstated on facilities. Vantage gets partial credit because campus count and MW/campus are close.

Q3.rationale: The public pure-play revenues for EQIX/DLR and GDS are roughly in range but miss required reconciliation details or use weak FX/constant-currency handling. NTT, IRM, and all private-operator revenues are far below the reference carve-outs and lack the required reverse-engineering/elimination support.

Q4.rationale: The answer generally applies the normalization in the wrong direction, increasing EBITDA rather than stripping adjustments. It also uses consolidated IRM EBITDA and greatly understates private-operator EBITDA without the required leverage-and-debt derivations.

Q5.rationale: This is the strongest section: it attempts blended and cohort PUEs with generally correct direction. However, several values are loose or wrong, design PUE is often missing, and the required NTT and IRM ESG/CDP scope inconsistencies are not properly flagged.

Q6.rationale: The answer presents annual and 24/7 figures side-by-side, but the hourly-match scores are systematically too high and Scope 2 location/market splits are missing or badly wrong for most entities. Several renewable percentages, especially IRM and QTS, materially contradict the reference.

Q7.rationale: The stress-test formula is wrong because it adds separate retention factors instead of applying the specified 30% in-sourcing shock. It also names wrong anchor customers for key entities and misses QTS as the highest-stress operator.

Q8.rationale: Some headline public capex figures are roughly in range, but capex/MW, capex/revenue, forward envelopes, and funding gaps are mostly wrong. The answer fails the key requirement to identify QTS as the largest absolute pipeline funding gap.

Where operators report only blended PUE, cohort split is estimated using:
